newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel sees debt deal details by March.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel sees debt deal details by March.

text.p: Eurotunnel Plc, the Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator, hopes to agree the details of its debt restructuring with the steering group of banks by March, chairman Patrick Ponsolle told Reuters on Monday.

The chairman said the company was one third of the way through negotiations of details to complete the documentation which will be sent to the entire banking syndicate behind Eurotunnel's debt of close to nine billion stg.

The news comes just before Eurotunnel is due to hold a press briefing on its 1996 review and the outlook for the current year, in the aftermath of a major tunnel fire last November, which hit Eurotunnel sales.

The group said earlier that its bank syndicate was seeking a debt standstill until December. Ponsolle told Reuters there was no deadline for banks to sign an agreement on the debt. But the chairman said it was in their interest to agree before the end of December.

Eurotunnel also hopes to have an answer from the French and UK governments on its request to extend its license to operate the tunnel in time for inclusion in the document which will be sent to its bankers.
The licence was extended in 1993 by 10 years. It was originally drawn up in 1985 and lasts for 65 years.
